ledger_excerpt:
From United States v. E. C. Knight Co., 156 U.S. 1, 12 (1895):
"Commerce succeeds to manufacture, and is not a part of it... The fact that an article is manufactured for export to another State does not of itself make it an article of interstate commerce..."   
From Mandeville Island Farms, Inc. v. American Crystal Sugar Co., 334 U.S. 219, 229–230, 235 (1948):
"The Knight decision made the statute a dead letter for more than a decade and, had its full momentum been gauged by the reasons assigned for the outcome, must have gone far toward defeating its purpose... The mechanical and unrealistic distinction between 'manufacture' and 'commerce' there taken has been repudiated by later decisions of this Court... [T]he amount of the nation's sugar industry which the refiners control is irrelevant, so long as control is exercised effectively in the area involved [and affects interstate commerce]."
